executiveSummary: Bloemendaal's generated identity, 2025 CBS totals, safety-region membership, five BAG woonplaatsen, two ProRail stations and 48 GTFS stop areas are coherent. The 22 neighbourhood population rows total 23,585, seven below the official 23,592 residents (-0.030%), consistent with independent CBS publication rounding; unavailable district-heating and charging fields remain null rather than zero. All ten canonical presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services, with exact-zero, finite-bound, causal-ledger, local allocation, reconciliation, cumulative-burden and selected-layer invariants passing. Release remains correction-required because locally operational spatial claims are unsupported. The coastal preset reports a 2.217045-metre municipality scalar, 14,887 affected people-equivalent and 100% inundation stress at T+24 without selecting a Rijnland defence failure, surge level, connected footprint, probability, arrival or dewatering curve. Coastal, pluvial, heat and wildfire maps reuse the identical synthetic neighbourhood order: Duinlustpark ranks first and Verspreide huizen Bloemendaal last, although that 1,699-hectare, 100-resident buurt contains much of the beach/dunes and 153 non-residential buildings. The municipal stress test instead identifies specific Bennebroek and Bloemendaal depressions, while VRK says more than half the municipality is dune/forest, summer beach use adds thousands of visitors and N200/N201 congestion constrains response. The canonical wildfire is a remote smoke/drought exercise with zero direct flame locally. Five N200/N206/N208 border links are also copied into all eight lifelines with nominal 150-unit capacities, not physical utility topology. Public registries remain context-only; unavailable or security-sensitive connectivity, capacity, telemetry, backup, staffing, stock and restoration are not fabricated.

evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025, table 86165NED, OData API
supports: A fresh official GM0377 row gives Bloemendaal, 23,592 residents, density 593 per square kilometre, 6,572 residents aged 65+ and 3,311 one-person households.
Municipality and neighbourhood attributes, plus CBS rounding, suppression and null semantics, support reconciliation without converting unavailable values to zero.

The OData table is machine-readable and reusable under CC BY 4.0; CBS labels it 2025 data, modified 25 June 2026, with quarterly additions where source variables become available. It is demographic context, not live occupancy, hazard exposure or response priority.

evidenceSources.title: CBS Gebiedsindelingen 2025 non-generalized geometry and national reference APIs
supports: Fresh full-resolution GM0377 is one component and one ring with 1,713 positions. The generated overview polygon retains that topology with 103 positions; estimated areas are 40.397 and 40.549 square kilometres, a 0.38% overview difference.

The generated centre and the five BAG woonplaatsen Aerdenhout, Bennebroek, Bloemendaal, Overveen and Vogelenzang are contained. Bloemendaal and Overveen stations, 48 GTFS stop areas and five N200/N206/N208 logical border links are represented.

CBS boundary OGC data are annual and CC BY 4.0; BAG is daily/Public Domain Mark, NWB is monthly/CC0 1.0, ProRail reference data are editioned/CC0, and GTFS has a feed-validity window. These are administrative, geometry and schedule context, not current people, closures, evacuation throughput or utility connectivity.
The non-generalized boundary, not the overview polygon, is required for intersecting dunes, defences, flood rasters, low points, roads and assets.

evidenceSources.title: Strategie en uitvoeringsagenda klimaatadaptatie Bloemendaal en Heemstede and Programma Water 2022–2026
supports: The municipal stress-test material identifies 10–20 centimetres of street water at De Ruyterlaan/Van Gendtlaan in Bennebroek, Iepenlaan/Platanenlaan/Kinheimweg and Lage Duin en Daalseweg/Arnoldlaan under its stated design rain assumptions.

The municipal water programme explains that local stress maps remain model results, that simply enlarging pumps has limited effect, and that sea influence generally moderates heat while cool-place access is broadly available.
The current municipal climate page documents separated rainwater collection, infiltration/drainage and temporary surface storage as relevant mechanisms.

These public pages/PDFs provide fixed policy and stress-test evidence, not live water depth or a standard machine export. No stable API, raster resolution, fixed refresh cadence or explicit standard reuse licence is stated; those metadata must be obtained before ingestion.

evidenceSources.title: Bloemendaal municipality risk page and Regionaal Risicoprofiel Kennemerland 2023–2030
supports: VRK states that more than half of Bloemendaal is dune and forest, including Natura 2000, and that longer drought makes these areas more susceptible to uncontrollable nature fire.

On summer days the beach and horeca attract thousands of visitors; congestion between Zandvoort, Bloemendaal, Heemstede and Haarlem on N200/N201 affects emergency-service deployment and access to beach, dune and forest.

The regional profile says coastal nature fire can trap people, threaten homes/care facilities, require large evacuation and external assistance, be difficult to access and take days to extinguish; it also recognizes flood, storm/cluster rain, heat/drought, electricity, gas, drinking-water, ICT and infrastructure cascades.

This is authoritative fixed planning evidence, not a live ignition, perimeter, visitor count, traffic feed, response-resource inventory or restoration promise. It exposes no standard machine API, fixed update cadence or explicit redistribution licence.

evidenceSources.title: Legger primaire waterkeringen and Bloemendaal beach/sea-defence policy
evidenceSources.edition: Current page; latest stated register actualization 2023
supports: The legal register records the position, required dimensions and maintenance responsibility for every dune and primary dike in Rijnland's management area and is updated regularly; the latest stated actualization was in 2023.
Rijnland identifies Bloemendaal's dunes as the primary North Sea defence and uses reach-specific modelling and future dune-growth zones in its beach policy.
Register/defence geometry is authoritative context, not present condition, breach probability, failed segment, surge, inundation footprint, arrival time or dewatering performance.
The public page and interactive register do not state a standard redistribution licence or contractual refresh interval; capture the governing decision, source version and terms before caching.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards via PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Waterschappen Kunstwerken IMWA and Waterketen DAMO OGC APIs
supports: The generated official-context intersection contains 19 water objects: three sewer pumps and 16 surface-water pumps, including named Bennebroek, Vogelenzang, Aerdenhout, Reigersbos, Bennebroekerpolder, De Bokkedoorns, Mariënduin and Parnassiakade context.

Kunstwerken IMWA and Waterketen DAMO are machine-readable OGC APIs and reusable under CC BY-SA 4.0; objects carry provider/source timestamps but contributor completeness varies and no single contractual refresh cadence is promised.

Point/register presence does not prove catchment connectivity, capacity, control logic, current availability, emergency power or restoration. The application correctly keeps these objects official-context with affectsSimulation=false.

evidenceSources.title: Natuurbranden — brandbaar natuurgebied WFS/WMS
supports: The public dataset delineates forest, heath and dune areas where a nature fire can arise and exposes OGC WFS/WMS through servicespub.risicokaart.nl.
Data.overheid identifies IPO as owner, Public Domain as licence and 19 February 2026 as the metadata update; no guaranteed operational refresh interval is stated.

This is integration-ready combustible-area eligibility/context, not an ignition, observed incident perimeter, fuel/moisture grid, spread forecast, evacuation zone or response state. No-data must remain unknown rather than non-burnable.

evidenceSources.title: Waterinfo and Landelijk Informatiesysteem Water en Overstromingen (LIWO)
supports: Waterinfo provides current, expected and historical water levels, waves, wind and related measurements with parameter/location-specific cadence; many water-level series are ten-minute observations.
LIWO is the official professional flood-planning system and its OGC services expose named maximum-depth, duration, warning-time, flow-speed and protected/unprotected coastal scenario layers.

Observations can support a timestamped replay and LIWO can support an expert-selected exercise footprint; neither is evidence that a defence has failed now. Layer id, event, probability, version, unit, resolution, CRS, issue/valid time, no-data and terms must be retained.
No guaranteed LIWO refresh cadence or explicit standard redistribution licence was established from the public service, so these remain review requirements rather than invented metadata.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six checkpoints across all eight services with complete finite output.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0377 pnpm audit:model passed one file/two tests in the final current-code rerun (29.51 seconds; 29.32 seconds in tests). A focused reproduction and headless browser workflow also passed.

Peak severity / maximum affected / T+72 attributable deprived person-hours are storm 0.298731 / 5,219 / 121,326.012; pluvial 0.300703 / 3,805 / 123,531.248; river 0 / 120 / 0; coastal 0.695633 / 14,887 / 738,663.256; heat 0.451862 / 2,338 / 81,095.239.

At T+24 coastal reports derived-screening inundation stress 2.217045, gust 28.861834 m/s and 14,887 affected people-equivalent. Compound reports rain 36.361966 mm/h, standing-water stress 0.234525, gust 22.848616 m/s and cyber disruption 0.526036, affecting 13,251.

The Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset has exact zero direct local forcing; its 120 T+72 affected-equivalent is an indirect logical-network state and produces zero event-attributable person-hours. Earthquake is a remote Groningen exercise; wildfire is a remote smoke/drought exercise with zero direct flame. Storm, pluvial, heat, winter, cyber and compound forcing are deterministic synthetic exercises, not observations or warnings.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact no-event semantics, local allocation, reconciliation, monotone burden and selected-layer invariance pass.
notes: All service availability stays in [0,1]; hazard dimensions, demand, delivery, affected people-equivalent and event-attributable person-hours remain finite and non-negative.

Repeated frames are deterministic, cumulative event-attributable burden never decreases, route flow respects effective capacity, and all eleven map-layer selections leave hazard, system pressure and affected population exactly invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One shared neighbourhood seed overrides documented coastal, pluvial, heat and dune-fire geography.
notes: At T+24 coastal, pluvial, heat and wildfire have the identical order: Duinlustpark, Bloemendaal, Oude Kern Bennebroek, Aerdenhout-Centrum and Leidsevaart-Bloemhof lead, while Verspreide huizen Bloemendaal is last.

The last-ranked neighbourhood has only 100 registered residents but covers 1,699 hectares, much of the beach/dunes, and 153 non-residential buildings. Coastal severity is 0.595266 there versus 0.800349 in Duinlustpark; the same rank repeats for physically unrelated hazards.
Meerwijk ranks 16/22 for pluvial exposure even though PDOK address geocoding places the municipality's named De Ruyterlaan/Van Gendtlaan depression in that Bennebroek neighbourhood.

The coastal scalar is derived from municipality-centre distance to a simplified coast and selects no defence segment, hydraulic connection, arrival or recession. The canonical remote wildfire has zero local direct flame and cannot test the locally defining dune ignition/access pathway.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight service balances calculate coherently, but identical road proxies replace physical sector topology and local visitor/facility dependencies.
notes: Compound T+24 availability is power 0.228466, water 0.511402, drainage 0.474036, gas 0.676006, telecom 0.374713, mobility 0.364291, facilities 0.673969 and supply 0.514054.

Every service exposes the same five N200/N206/N208 route IDs, each with nominal 150-unit capacity and transferSemantics logical-proxy. Flow differs, but no source establishes roads as electricity, drinking-water, drainage, gas, telecom or facility transfer edges.

Even with zero local river forcing, T+72 pressure is 0.143615, drainage availability 0.712977 and 120 modeled people-equivalent are under pressure through indirect proxy-network state; this is not evidence of a Rijnland, PWN, Liander or operator outage.
Public pump, provider, cable, station, facility and transit geometry can scope responsibility/context, but does not safely supply connectivity, capacity, current state, backup or restoration.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality explanation ledgers close and the UI exposes scenario versus derived-screening evidence without making public context causal.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; each service baseline plus ordered stage deltas sums to availability; eight weighted service-pressure contributions sum to municipality system pressure.

Drivers, dependencies, interventions, local demand/vulnerability terms and restoration counterfactuals are finite and arithmetically closed. Preparedness changes modeled consequences after physical pressure rather than altering hazard fragility.

At coastal T+24 the browser displays 'Scenario · evidence class derived-screening' and an explicit RWS/ROR/HWH caveat saying the visible registers are not a selected breach/depth/arrival/performance scenario.

A 1440×1000 headless Chromium path loaded without page/console/local-response errors, selected Bloemendaal, coastal T+24 and the dune neighbourhood by map click, then exposed the remote-wildfire zero-flame state. Initial readiness was 0.993 s, municipality 0.085 s, scenario 0.125 s, checkpoint 1.801 s and drilldown 0.774 s; timings are diagnostics, not hazard evidence.

recovery72h.summary: Sustained standing water correctly blocks repair, but coastal recession/dewatering and all operator restoration magnitudes remain uncalibrated.
notes: Compound retains 0.234525 standing-water stress and 0.068416 cyber disruption at T+72, remains critical with 13,882 affected people-equivalent and keeps all eight recoveryProgress values at zero.

Coastal direct water and wind forcing are zero by T+72, yet 1,091 remain modeled under pressure; service recovery ranges 0.491877–0.953366 and availability 0.588932–0.928890 without a defence, surge hydrograph, breach closure, drainage/dewatering, access or operator repair model.
Storm, pluvial, winter, earthquake and wildfire forcing has ended by T+72 without reducing cumulative attributable person-hours; heat/cyber follow their preset schedules.
The corrected zero-intensity and sustained-flood mechanics work as designed, but no source validates Bloemendaal's precise recovery percentage or timing.

findings.evidence: At T+24 the preset reports 2.217045 m, 14,887 affected people-equivalent, critical status and 100% inundation stress; T+72 burden reaches 738,663.256 person-hours. Rijnland identifies a primary dune defence and reach-specific policy, but the model selects no segment/state, surge, probability, connected footprint, arrival, duration or dewatering curve.

Meerwijk ranks 16/22 for pluvial exposure although municipal evidence identifies De Ruyterlaan/Van Gendtlaan water depressions there. The same order cannot represent coast/defence connectivity, low points, urban heat and ignition/smoke geometry simultaneously.

VRK says more than half the municipality is dune/forest and highlights entrapment, evacuation, difficult access, large crew demand and multi-day extinguishing; the dune neighbourhood nevertheless ranks last under the shared seed.
findings.action: Keep the preset labelled remote smoke and add a separately named local dune-fire exercise using IPO combustible-area geometry and event-valid KNMI weather; where no public incident/spread feed exists, use the smallest transparent versioned synthetic ignition/perimeter and never imply an observed fire.

The dune/beach neighbourhood has only 100 registered residents but 153 non-residential buildings and multiple beach stops; modeled exposure, facility demand and route pressure remain resident-seeded and season-insensitive to an explicit visitor load.
findings.action: Add a clearly sourced day/time visitor-demand scenario using public municipal/GTFS/NDW/approved count data where terms permit; otherwise publish a transparent scenario range. Keep current traffic observations time-stamped and distinct from simulated T+0–72 demand.

Context contains zero RIVM acute-care locations, 19 DUO education uses and five government points, but none provides shelter activation, attendance, staffing, generator endurance, supplies, accessibility or transfer capacity. findings.evidence: The focused gate covers ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Values are finite/deterministic, zero intensity is exact, local totals reconcile, causal ledgers close, cumulative burden is monotone, layer selection is invariant and continuing compound water blocks premature restoration.

corrections.summary: Replace GM0377's generic coastal scalar with a selected defence-dependent hydraulic scenario while preserving unknown/no-data semantics.
corrections.validation: Best public sources are RWS/WMCN LIWO OGC at https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows (named depth, duration, flow and warning-time scenario grids; layer-specific resolution/version; no guaranteed cadence or explicit standard redistribution licence established), Rijnland's primary-defence register at https://www.rijnland.net/zakelijk/legger/legger-primaire-keringen/ (object/reach legal geometry, updated regularly with latest stated actualization 2023; licence identifier/contractual interval unstated), and Waterinfo parameter-specific, often ten-minute observations. Clip with annual non-generalized PDOK CBS geometry (CC BY 4.0), never the overview polygon. Require expert selection of event, defence segment/state, surge, probability, depth unit, arrival/recession, CRS, resolution, no-data, issue/valid time and terms. Until approved, direct depth/exposure remains unknown. If no releasable scenario exists, use one smallest named/versioned synthetic failure footprint and label all dependent output hypothetical.

corrections.summary: Integrate local pluvial/heat terrain evidence and remove the shared neighbourhood ordering.
corrections.validation: First obtain the municipality's stress-test rasters behind its adopted strategy for De Ruyterlaan/Van Gendtlaan, Iepenlaan/Platanenlaan/Kinheimweg and Lage Duin en Daalseweg/Arnoldlaan; the public PDF/page has no stable machine export, raster resolution, refresh cadence or standard licence, so confirm these before caching. Use PDOK AHN WMS/WCS https://service.pdok.nl/rws/ahn/wcs/v1_0 (0.5-m latest mosaic; open-data service, licence version to be recorded from metadata) and BGT daily CC0 surfaces only as covariates/flow-path context, not observed water. Klimaateffectatlas WMS/GeoTIFF/GeoPackage https://www.klimaateffectatlas.nl/nl/faq is CC BY 4.0 and updated several times per year, but its publisher says national maps are unsuitable for local decisions; use as explicit screening only. Bind KNMI Data Platform radar/weather files (5-/10-minute products, notifications, CC BY 4.0) to named replay valid times, never as simulated depth. Validate no-data != zero, Meerwijk/local hotspot differentiation, exact allocation and stable source metadata.

corrections.summary: Add a separately named local dune-fire/visitor-access exercise without converting land cover or current traffic into an incident forecast.
corrections.validation: Use IPO/Risicokaart brandbaar natuurgebied WFS https://servicespub.risicokaart.nl/geoserver/ISOR_RK/wfs?service=WFS&request=GetCapabilities (forest/heath/dune polygons, Public Domain, metadata updated 19 February 2026, no guaranteed incident cadence) only as an ignition-eligibility mask. Use KNMI event-valid 5-/10-minute wind, humidity and temperature (CC BY 4.0, file/product cadence) for a named replay. Use RWS NWB monthly CC0, NDW timestamped DATEX II observations and feed-valid GTFS only for matched access/reference; none supplies evacuation capacity. VRK planning evidence has no machine cadence/licence and is not a perimeter. No reviewed public source provides a local live fire-spread, fuel-moisture, visitor-occupancy or response-resource feed, so fallback must be a smallest versioned synthetic ignition/perimeter plus explicit visitor-demand range, escape/access and suppression-water assumptions. Test zero flame outside the footprint and prevent a shared seed from relocating it.

corrections.summary: Separate mobility/supply routes from safe aggregate electricity, water, drainage, gas, telecom and facility networks.
corrections.validation: For mobility/supply use RWS NWB OGC https://api.pdok.nl/rws/nationaal-wegenbestand-wegen/ogc/v1 (monthly, CC0 1.0), event-valid NDW DATEX II (timestamped observed state; CC0 where dataset metadata states it), ProRail reference geometry (editioned/CC0) and OVapi GTFS (feed-validity cadence) with explicit beach/N200 access matching; none alone gives throughput or evacuation capacity. For drainage/water use HWH IMWA/DAMO OGC https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 (CC BY-SA 4.0, provider-supplied timestamps, variable completeness) only as topology context until connectivity/capacity is authorized. Liander ArcGIS geometry is CC BY 4.0, fixed cadence unstated and territory-limited; Stichting Mijn Aansluiting provider WMS/WFS is Public Domain with provider-specific timestamps and partial/overlapping disciplines. No reviewed public source safely supplies complete PWN, sewer, electricity, gas, telecom, facility, stock, backup or restoration topology, so use clearly synthetic service-specific aggregate nodes and never reuse road IDs outside mobility/supply.

corrections.summary: Add safe facility-role/continuity context without inventing live capacity for Bloemendaal's older residents or visitors.
corrections.validation: Retain RIVM 2026 emergency-department questionnaire locations (CC0, dated annual questionnaire release), daily DUO RIO education uses (Creative Commons Attribution, version unstated) and KVK/PDOK government-service points (Public Domain Mark) as official context only; GM0377 currently has zero RIVM acute-care locations, 19 education uses and five government points. BAG daily/Public Domain Mark building/use-purpose data can add structural context but not shelter role. Request authorized municipality/VRK safe aggregate shelter, care, cooling-site and continuity interfaces with issue time and access terms. If none is public, keep activation, occupancy, staffing, accessible transport, generator/fuel endurance, supplies and patient-transfer capacity unknown and retain a plainly synthetic aggregate facilities index.

residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, emergency instruction, flood assessment, evacuation plan, wildfire forecast or operator commitment.
CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed and neighbourhood totals need not equal the municipality total; null district-heating, charging and car indicators are unknown, not zero.
Resident population excludes present beach, park, horeca, school, station and event visitors; no authoritative timestamped occupancy is consumed.
The overview boundary is suitable for selection, not for coast, dune, defence, raster, low-point, road, catchment or asset intersection; use full-resolution PDOK geometry.
Rijnland defence registers describe legal/physical context, not condition, failure, live level, footprint, probability, arrival, flow or dewatering performance.

LIWO and Klimaateffectatlas layers are modeled scenarios/screens and require expert selection, version, units, resolution, probability/no-data semantics, reuse terms and local validation before causal use.
Waterinfo and KNMI observations/nowcasts can support provenance or a named replay but do not create a generic T+72 forecast, inundation surface, fire perimeter, outage or restoration path.
VRK profiles are planning evidence; they do not expose live visitors, traffic, crews, evacuation capacity, facility state, extinguishing water or incident perimeters.
